q: Cells divide on a regular basic to bring about growth and ____.
e: Cells divide on a regular basic to bring about growth and asexual reproduction. Asexual reproduction copies one parent, often through mitosis.

q: The cell cycle involves several different phases, including Interphase and the ____.
e: The cell cycle involves several different phases, including Interphase and the mitotic M phase. The cell cycle is growth plus nuclear and cytoplasmic division. The cell cycle is the ordered sequence of growth, DNA copy, and division.

q: Interphase is subdivided into G$_1$, S and ____ stages.
e: Interphase is subdivided into G1, S and G2 stages. G2 is the growth and check stage after DNA has been copied. S is the synthesis stage of interphase when DNA is copied.

q: In G$_1$ stage, the ____ of cell takes place.
e: In G1 stage, the growth of cell takes place. Growth is the biological term this statement needs.

q: DNA replication is carried out in ____ stage.
e: DNA replication is carried out in S stage. DNA replication happens in S phase. DNA carries the genetic code in a double helix of nucleotides.

q: After replication is completed each chromosome consists of two identical DNA molecules called ____.
e: After replication is completed each chromosome consists of two identical DNA molecules called chromatids. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere. A chromosome is a DNA molecule with proteins, visible when condensed.

q: Chromatids are joined together at a point called the ____.
e: Chromatids are joined together at a point called the centromere. The centromere is where sister chromatids are held and where spindle fibres attach. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere.

q: In G$_2$ stage, the organelles are replicated and the ____ grows.
e: In G2 stage, the organelles are replicated and the cell grows. The cell is the basic living unit of structure and function.

q: This is followed by mitosis, a period of active nuclear division and ____, the separation of cytoplasm.
e: This is followed by mitosis, a period of active nuclear division and cytokinesis, the separation of cytoplasm. Cytokinesis splits the cytoplasm to finish making two cells. Cytoplasm is the fluid and structures inside the cell membrane, around the nucleus.

q: Cell division is a strictly regulated process that mostly works without errors. When errors do occur, they can be catastrophic and cause the development of ____.
e: Cell division is a strictly regulated process that mostly works without errors. When errors do occur, they can be catastrophic and cause the development of cancer. Cancer is uncontrolled cell division after control checkpoints fail.

q: Interphase, the initial stage of the cell cycle, used to be called the ____ phase.
e: Interphase, the initial stage of the cell cycle, used to be called the resting phase. The cell cycle is growth plus nuclear and cytoplasmic division. The cell cycle is the ordered sequence of growth, DNA copy, and division.

q: Actually, it is not resting during interphase; the normal metabolic processes of the cell continue and new DNA is produced for the replication of ____.
e: Actually, it is not resting during interphase; the normal metabolic processes of the cell continue and new DNA is produced for the replication of chromosome. A chromosome is a DNA molecule with proteins, visible when condensed. Interphase is G1, S, and G2, when the cell grows and copies DNA.

q: New proteins, cytoplasm and cell organelles are also made so that the cell is in the state of preparation to produce ____.
e: New proteins, cytoplasm and cell organelles are also made so that the cell is in the state of preparation to produce two new cells. The cell is the basic living unit; tissues are groups of similar cells. Many metabolic reactions run in the cytoplasm.

q: During the process of cell division, the chromosomes that are duplicated during interphase are divided with the remaining contents of the cell to produce two identical ____.
e: During the process of cell division, the chromosomes that are duplicated during interphase are divided with the remaining contents of the cell to produce two identical daughter cells. Mitosis plus cytokinesis yields two genetically identical daughter cells. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells.

q: Mitosis is divided into four phases: prophase, metaphase, anaphase and ____.
e: Mitosis is divided into four phases: prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase. In telophase nuclei reform around the two chromosome sets. In metaphase chromosomes line up on the metaphase plate.

q: In prophase, the chromatins become more tightly coiled and condensing into discrete ____.
e: In prophase, the chromatins become more tightly coiled and condensing into discrete chromosomes. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells. In prophase chromosomes condense and the spindle starts to form.

q: Each early mitotic chromosome appears as two identical sister chromatids joined at their ____.
e: Each early mitotic chromosome appears as two identical sister chromatids joined at their centromeres. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere. A chromosome is a DNA molecule with proteins, visible when condensed.

q: The spindles begin to form. The radial arrays of shorter microtubules around each centriole are called ____.
e: The spindles begin to form. The radial arrays of shorter microtubules around each centriole are called asters. Asters are microtubule arrays around the poles in animal mitosis.

q: The centrioles start moving to opposite ends of the cell, forming protein fibres between them called the ____.
e: The centrioles start moving to opposite ends of the cell, forming protein fibres between them called the spindles. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs.

q: The nuclear envelope breaks down and the ____ disappears.
e: The nuclear envelope breaks down and the nucleolus disappears. The nucleolus vanishes in prophase and returns in telophase. The nuclear envelope breaks down in prophase and reforms in telophase.

q: In metaphase, the chromosomes line up along the ____ of the cell.
e: In metaphase, the chromosomes line up along the metaphase plate of the cell. The metaphase plate is the equator where chromosomes align. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells.

q: Each chromatid becomes attached to the spindle by its ____.
e: Each chromatid becomes attached to the spindle by its centromere. The centromere is where sister chromatids are held and where spindle fibres attach. Sister chromatids stay attached at the centromere.

q: In anaphase, the chromatids from each pair are pulled, ____ first, towards opposite poles of the cell.
e: In anaphase, the chromatids from each pair are pulled, centromere first, towards opposite poles of the cell. The centromere is where sister chromatids are held and where spindle fibres attach. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere.

q: The centromeres divide, separating each pair of sister chromatids, due to contraction of ____.
e: The centromeres divide, separating each pair of sister chromatids, due to contraction of spindles. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere.

q: At the end of anaphase, the two sets of chromatids have been separated to opposite ends of the cell. The chromatids are now called ____.
e: At the end of anaphase, the two sets of chromatids have been separated to opposite ends of the cell. The chromatids are now called chromosomes. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere.

q: During telophase, the spindle fibres break down and ____ reform around the two sets of chromosomes.
e: During telophase, the spindle fibres break down and nuclear envelopes reform around the two sets of chromosomes. Two nuclear envelopes form in telophase. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells.

q: The ____ and centrioles are also re-formed.
e: The nucleoli and centrioles are also re-formed. Nucleoli is the biological term this statement needs.

q: The chromosomes begin to uncoil and becoming less dense, as in Figure 5.6.
e: The chromosomes begin to uncoil and becoming less dense, as in Figure 5.6. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells.

q: In animal cells, a ring of contractile fibres tightens around the centre of the cell similar to a belt tightening around a sack of ____.
e: In animal cells, a ring of contractile fibres tightens around the centre of the cell similar to a belt tightening around a sack of flour. Flour is the biological term this statement needs.

q: In plant cells, the division for the cell occurs differently. A ____ cell wall builds up from the inside of the cell outwards.
e: In plant cells, the division for the cell occurs differently. A cellulose cell wall builds up from the inside of the cell outwards. Cellulose is the beta-glucose polymer that makes plant cell walls rigid. The cell is the basic living unit of structure and function.

q: In both cases, the result is that two genetically identical ____ are formed.
e: In both cases, the result is that two genetically identical daughter cells are formed. Mitosis plus cytokinesis yields two genetically identical daughter cells. Mitosis makes genetically identical body cells for growth and repair.

q: Meiosis is a type of nuclear division that happens only in ____.
e: Meiosis is a type of nuclear division that happens only in sex organs. Meiosis is reduction division that makes haploid gametes and shuffles alleles.

q: Cells that divide by meiosis have the full number of chromosomes to start with, but the cells that are formed from meiosis have half the number. So it is called ____.
e: Cells that divide by meiosis have the full number of chromosomes to start with, but the cells that are formed from meiosis have half the number. So it is called reduction division. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells.

q: In animals, the gametes are formed directly from meiosis. The formation of sperm is called spermatogenesis, while that of ovum is called ____.
e: In animals, the gametes are formed directly from meiosis. The formation of sperm is called spermatogenesis, while that of ovum is called oogenesis. Oogenesis is meiosis that produces eggs. Spermatogenesis is meiosis that produces sperm.

q: In flowering plants, meiosis forms special male cells called microspores and female cells called ____.
e: In flowering plants, meiosis forms special male cells called microspores and female cells called megaspores. Flowering is the mark of angiosperms. Meiosis is reduction division that makes haploid gametes and shuffles alleles.

q: In meiosis, two nuclear divisions produce four ____ daughter cells.
e: In meiosis, two nuclear divisions produce four haploid daughter cells. Haploid cells have one set of chromosomes, as in gametes. Mitosis plus cytokinesis yields two genetically identical daughter cells.

q: No chromosome replication occurs between meiosis I and ____.
e: No chromosome replication occurs between meiosis I and meiosis II. Meiosis is reduction division that makes haploid gametes and shuffles alleles. Meiosis halves the chromosome number for gametes.

q: In prophase I of meiosis, the two chromosomes of each pair, known as homologous pairs, stay close together in a process called ____.
e: In prophase I of meiosis, the two chromosomes of each pair, known as homologous pairs, stay close together in a process called synapsis. Synapsis is pairing of homologous chromosomes in meiosis I. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells.

q: At this stage, ____ introduces genetic variation as the chromatids may break and recombine.
e: At this stage, crossing over introduces genetic variation as the chromatids may break and recombine. Crossing over in prophase I swaps DNA between homologous chromosomes. Meiosis, crossing over, and random fertilisation generate genetic variation.

q: In anaphase I, the centromeres do not divide. One chromosome (pair of chromatids) from each homologous pair moves to each end of the cell. As a result, the chromosome number at each pole is ____ to that of the original numbers.
e: In anaphase I, the centromeres do not divide. One chromosome (pair of chromatids) from each homologous pair moves to each end of the cell. As a result, the chromosome number at each pole is half to that of the original numbers. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere.

q: In telophase I, the nuclear membrane re-forms and the cells begin to ____.
e: In telophase I, the nuclear membrane re-forms and the cells begin to divide. In telophase nuclei reform around the two chromosome sets.

q: The branch of biology known as Genetics deals with the inheritance of characteristics or traits from parents to their ____.
e: The branch of biology known as Genetics deals with the inheritance of characteristics or traits from parents to their progeny. Biology systematically studies plants, animals, and microorganisms.

q: These characteristics are controlled by genes located in DNA molecules inside ____.
e: These characteristics are controlled by genes located in DNA molecules inside chromosomes. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells. DNA carries the genetic code in a double helix of nucleotides.

q: The physical and chemical characteristics that make up the appearance of an organism are known as its ____.
e: The physical and chemical characteristics that make up the appearance of an organism are known as its phenotype. Phenotype is the observed trait produced by genotype and environment.

q: The phenotype of an individual is determined by its ____.
e: The phenotype of an individual is determined by its genotype. Genotype is the allele combination an organism carries. Phenotype is the observed trait produced by genotype and environment.

q: Genes are unit of hereditary ____.
e: Genes are unit of hereditary characteristics. Characteristics is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Each gene is always located in the same place on one of the ____.
e: Each gene is always located in the same place on one of the chromosomes. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells. A gene is a DNA stretch that codes for a product, usually a protein.

q: The different forms of each gene are known as ____.
e: The different forms of each gene are known as alleles. Alleles are different versions of the same gene. A gene is a DNA stretch that codes for a product, usually a protein.

q: If the two alleles are different, the individual is ____ to this gene.
e: If the two alleles are different, the individual is heterozygous to this gene. Heterozygous means the two alleles of a gene are different. Alleles are different versions of the same gene.

q: If the two alleles are the same, the individual is ____ dominant.
e: If the two alleles are the same, the individual is homozygous dominant. Homozygous means both alleles of a gene are the same. A dominant allele shows in the phenotype even when only one copy is present.

q: If the two alleles are the same and recessive, the individual is homozygous recessive and the recessive allele will be expressed in the ____.
e: If the two alleles are the same and recessive, the individual is homozygous recessive and the recessive allele will be expressed in the phenotype. Phenotype is the observed trait produced by genotype and environment. Homozygous means both alleles of a gene are the same.

q: Some well-known patterns of inheritance are: (i) Dominance (ii) Codominance (iii) Incomplete dominance (iv) ____.
e: Some well-known patterns of inheritance are: (i) Dominance (ii) Codominance (iii) Incomplete dominance (iv) Multiple alleles. Multiple alleles means a gene has more than two possible versions in the population, as in ABO blood groups. Incomplete dominance blends the heterozygote, as in pink from red and white.

q: Gregor J. Mendel (1822–1884), an Austrian monk, discovered laws of inheritance, based on results of breeding experiments on a ____ plant.
e: Gregor J. Mendel (1822–1884), an Austrian monk, discovered laws of inheritance, based on results of breeding experiments on a garden pea plant. Mendel used the garden pea because it has clear traits and controlled crosses.

q: A monofactorial cross demonstrates Mendel's principle of ____.
e: A monofactorial cross demonstrates Mendel's principle of segregation. Segregation is the splitting of allele pairs when gametes form.

q: The law of segregation states that during the formation of gametes, the two traits carried by each parent ____.
e: The law of segregation states that during the formation of gametes, the two traits carried by each parent separate. Segregation is the splitting of allele pairs when gametes form. Gametes are sex cells: sperm and eggs, produced by meiosis.

q: Each true-breeding plant of the parental generation has two identical alleles, denoted as either PP or ____.
e: Each true-breeding plant of the parental generation has two identical alleles, denoted as either PP or pp. Alleles are different versions of the same gene. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: Because the purple-flower allele is dominant, all F$_1$ hybrids have ____ flowers.
e: Because the purple-flower allele is dominant, all F1 hybrids have purple flowers. A dominant allele shows in the phenotype even when only one copy is present. Alleles are different versions of the same gene.

q: Random combination of the gametes results in the ____ ratio in the F$_2$ generation.
e: Random combination of the gametes results in the 3:1 ratio in the F2 generation. A monohybrid heterozygous cross gives a 3:1 phenotypic ratio in the F2. Gametes are sex cells: sperm and eggs, produced by meiosis.

q: A dihybrid cross is used to show the inheritance of two different characteristics, controlled by two genes, which may be located on different pairs of ____.
e: A dihybrid cross is used to show the inheritance of two different characteristics, controlled by two genes, which may be located on different pairs of homologous chromosomes. Homologous chromosomes pair in meiosis; they carry the same genes but may have different alleles. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells.

q: Mendel's second law (Law of independent assortment) states that during gamete formation, the genes for one trait are not inherited along with the genes for another ____.
e: Mendel's second law (Law of independent assortment) states that during gamete formation, the genes for one trait are not inherited along with the genes for another trait. Independent assortment is the random sorting of different chromosome pairs into gametes.

q: The only factor that determines how these alleles are inherited is how the homologous pairs happen to line up in metaphase of meiosis I, which is a ____ event.
e: The only factor that determines how these alleles are inherited is how the homologous pairs happen to line up in metaphase of meiosis I, which is a random event. In metaphase chromosomes line up on the metaphase plate. Meiosis is reduction division that makes haploid gametes and shuffles alleles.

q: Testcross is used to determine the genotype of an individual exhibiting a ____ phenotype.
e: Testcross is used to determine the genotype of an individual exhibiting a dominant phenotype. A dominant allele shows in the phenotype even when only one copy is present. Phenotype is the observed trait produced by genotype and environment.

q: The testcross parent is always homozygous ____ for all of the genes under consideration.
e: The testcross parent is always homozygous recessive for all of the genes under consideration. A recessive allele shows only when two copies are present. Homozygous means both alleles of a gene are the same.

q: A homozygous dominant individual will produce only one kind of ____.
e: A homozygous dominant individual will produce only one kind of gamete. Homozygous means both alleles of a gene are the same. A dominant allele shows in the phenotype even when only one copy is present.

q: Backcross is done in order to achieve offspring with a genotype closer to that of the ____.
e: Backcross is done in order to achieve offspring with a genotype closer to that of the parents. Genotype is the allele combination an organism carries.

q: In the backcross, the F$_1$ progeny are mated back to one of their parents (or to individuals with a genotype identical to that of their ____).
e: In the backcross, the F1 progeny are mated back to one of their parents (or to individuals with a genotype identical to that of their parents). Genotype is the allele combination an organism carries.

q: Alleles that lack complete dominant and recessive relationships and are both observed phenotypically are called ____.
e: Alleles that lack complete dominant and recessive relationships and are both observed phenotypically are called codominant. Codominant alleles both show fully in the heterozygote, as in AB blood. A recessive allele shows only when two copies are present.

q: Coat colours of the Shorthorn breed of cattle represent a classical example of ____ allele.
e: Coat colours of the Shorthorn breed of cattle represent a classical example of codominant allele. Codominant alleles both show fully in the heterozygote, as in AB blood. Alleles are different versions of the same gene.

q: Red is governed by the genotype C$^R$C$^R$ and white by ____.
e: Red is governed by the genotype C^RC^R and white by C^WC^W. Genotype is the allele combination an organism carries.

q: When red shorthorns are crossed with white shorthorns, ____ (mixture of red and white) are produced.
e: When red shorthorns are crossed with white shorthorns, roan (mixture of red and white) are produced. Roan coat is a classic codominance of red and white hairs.

q: If a dominant allele of a gene does not completely mask the effects of its recessive allele, the organism's phenotype shows a blending of both alleles. This is called ____.
e: If a dominant allele of a gene does not completely mask the effects of its recessive allele, the organism's phenotype shows a blending of both alleles. This is called incomplete dominance. Phenotype is the observed trait produced by genotype and environment.

q: When pink-flowered plants are crossed together, all three phenotypes reappear, in the ratio of 1 red : 2 pink : ____.
e: When pink-flowered plants are crossed together, all three phenotypes reappear, in the ratio of 1 red: 2 pink: 1 white. Dichotomous does not mean divided into three parts.

q: When there are more than two alleles of the genes, it is refer to as ____.
e: When there are more than two alleles of the genes, it is refer to as multiple alleles. Multiple alleles means a gene has more than two possible versions in the population, as in ABO blood groups. Alleles are different versions of the same gene.

q: A classical example of multiple alleles is found in the ABO blood group system of ____.
e: A classical example of multiple alleles is found in the ABO blood group system of humans. ABO blood groups come from multiple alleles of one gene. Multiple alleles means a gene has more than two possible versions in the population, as in ABO blood groups.

q: The allele I$^A$ for the A antigen is codominant with the allele I$^B$ for the B ____.
e: The allele I^A for the A antigen is codominant with the allele I^B for the B antigen. An antigen is a molecule the immune system can recognise. Codominant alleles both show fully in the heterozygote, as in AB blood.

q: Both I$^A$ and I$^B$ are completely dominant to the allele i, which fails to specify any detectable antigenic ____.
e: Both I^A and I^B are completely dominant to the allele i, which fails to specify any detectable antigenic structure. Structure is the form and arrangement of parts in an organism. A dominant allele shows in the phenotype even when only one copy is present.

q: The blood group AB is referred as universal ____.
e: The blood group AB is referred as universal recipient. AB is the universal recipient for red cells because it has no anti-A or anti-B. ABO blood groups come from multiple alleles of one gene.

q: Blood group O can transfuse to any of all four groups, as it has neither A antigen nor B antigen, making it the universal ____.
e: Blood group O can transfuse to any of all four groups, as it has neither A antigen nor B antigen, making it the universal donor. O is the universal donor for red cells because it lacks A and B antigens. ABO blood groups come from multiple alleles of one gene.

q: In man, and apparently in all other mammals, the presence of the Y chromosome may determine a tendency to ____.
e: In man, and apparently in all other mammals, the presence of the Y chromosome may determine a tendency to maleness. The Y chromosome carries factors for maleness. A chromosome is a DNA molecule with proteins, visible when condensed.

q: Normal males are chromosomally XY and females are ____.
e: Normal males are chromosomally XY and females are XX. XX is the typical human female sex-chromosome pair.

q: Since the male produces two kinds of gametes as far as the sex chromosomes are concerned, he is said to be the ____ sex.
e: Since the male produces two kinds of gametes as far as the sex chromosomes are concerned, he is said to be the heterogametic sex. Human males are heterogametic because they make X and Y sperm. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells.

q: A mutation is a change in a gene or a chromosome that may cause a change in a ____ characteristic.
e: A mutation is a change in a gene or a chromosome that may cause a change in a phenotypic characteristic. A chromosome is a DNA molecule with proteins, visible when condensed. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait.

q: Mutations that occur in body cells will only affect the particular cell in which they ____.
e: Mutations that occur in body cells will only affect the particular cell in which they occur. Occur is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Only mutation in sex cells (gametes), or in the cell that divide to form gametes, can be passed on to the next generation and genetic diseases can be ____.
e: Only mutation in sex cells (gametes), or in the cell that divide to form gametes, can be passed on to the next generation and genetic diseases can be formed. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait. Gametes are sex cells: sperm and eggs, produced by meiosis.

q: Bits of chromosomes can sometimes break off from one chromosome and become attached to another. These 'mistakes' are called ____.
e: Bits of chromosomes can sometimes break off from one chromosome and become attached to another. These 'mistakes' are called chromosome mutations. Chromosome mutations change structure or number of whole chromosomes. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells.

q: One relatively common chromosome mutation results in ova containing two copies of chromosome ____.
e: One relatively common chromosome mutation results in ova containing two copies of chromosome 21. A chromosome is a DNA molecule with proteins, visible when condensed. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait.

q: The zygote will have three copies of chromosome 21. This is called trisomy of chromosome ____.
e: The zygote will have three copies of chromosome 21. This is called trisomy of chromosome 21. A chromosome is a DNA molecule with proteins, visible when condensed. Dichotomous does not mean divided into three parts.

q: The condition that results is Down's ____.
e: The condition that results is Down's syndrome. An extra chromosome 21 produces Down's syndrome.

q: Down's syndrome is more common in babies born by women over ____ years of age than by younger women.
e: Down's syndrome is more common in babies born by women over 40 years of age than by younger women. Down's syndrome comes from an extra chromosome 21. An extra chromosome 21 produces Down's syndrome.

q: A change in the nucleotide sequences of a DNA molecule is termed as ____.
e: A change in the nucleotide sequences of a DNA molecule is termed as gene mutation. A gene mutation changes the base sequence of one gene. A nucleotide is a sugar, a phosphate, and a nitrogen base.

q: The order of DNA bases in a gene determines the order of amino acids in a particular ____.
e: The order of DNA bases in a gene determines the order of amino acids in a particular protein. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Amino acids have an amine group and a carboxyl group around a central carbon.

q: If a mutation occurs in a gene, the primary structure of the protein it codes for could be ____.
e: If a mutation occurs in a gene, the primary structure of the protein it codes for could be altered. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs.

q: Albinism is caused by a mutation in the gene that codes for the enzyme that produce ____.
e: Albinism is caused by a mutation in the gene that codes for the enzyme that produce melanin. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed reactions without being used up.

q: Cystic fibrosis is caused by a mutation in the gene that codes for CFTR protein that transport ____ ions.
e: Cystic fibrosis is caused by a mutation in the gene that codes for CFTR protein that transport chloride ions. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs.

q: Sickle-cell anemia is caused by a mutation in the gene that codes for the B-chain of ____.
e: Sickle-cell anemia is caused by a mutation in the gene that codes for the B-chain of haemoglobin. Haemoglobin in red blood cells binds oxygen for transport. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait.

q: Huntington's disease is caused by a mutation in HD gene located on chromosome ____.
e: Huntington's disease is caused by a mutation in HD gene located on chromosome 4. A chromosome is a DNA molecule with proteins, visible when condensed. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait.

q: Mutations are caused by damage to DNA or by a failure in the DNA copying process that occurs before nuclear division in ____.
e: Mutations are caused by damage to DNA or by a failure in the DNA copying process that occurs before nuclear division in cells. The cell is the basic living unit; tissues are groups of similar cells. DNA carries the genetic code in a double helix of nucleotides.

q: Ultra-violet radiation, X-rays and gamma rays are the most damaging ____.
e: Ultra-violet radiation, X-rays and gamma rays are the most damaging radiation. Radiation is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Benzpyrene in cigarette smoke causes ____.
e: Benzpyrene in cigarette smoke causes mutation. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait.

q: The agents that cause mutation are called ____.
e: The agents that cause mutation are called mutagens. Physical mutagens include radiation; chemical mutagens include some drugs and pollutants. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait.

q: Variation is the differences that exist within a ____.
e: Variation is the differences that exist within a species. A species is a group of organisms that can breed to produce fertile offspring.

q: Gene mutation is the only way in which completely new genetic material is ____.
e: Gene mutation is the only way in which completely new genetic material is produced. A gene mutation changes the base sequence of one gene. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait.

q: During meiosis, the alleles of different genes are 'shuffled' to give new combinations in the ____.
e: During meiosis, the alleles of different genes are 'shuffled' to give new combinations in the gametes. Gametes are sex cells: sperm and eggs, produced by meiosis. Meiosis is reduction division that makes haploid gametes and shuffles alleles.

q: Gene mutation, meiosis and fertilization give rise to variation between individuals in every ____.
e: Gene mutation, meiosis and fertilization give rise to variation between individuals in every generation. A gene mutation changes the base sequence of one gene. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait.

q: Continuous variation shows no clear cut distinction between the different traits of a characteristic, e.g. height, weight, intelligence, skin colour, number of seeds in a ____.
e: Continuous variation shows no clear cut distinction between the different traits of a characteristic, e.g. Height, weight, intelligence, skin colour, number of seeds in a pod. Continuous culture keeps adding nutrients and taking product for a long run. Skin is a surface for some heat exchange and a barrier, but most large animals also need lungs or gills.

q: Discontinuous variation shows a clear cut distinction between two traits, e.g. eye and skin colour (pigmented or non-pigmented), left-handed/right-handed, ability/inability to roll the ____.
e: Discontinuous variation shows a clear cut distinction between two traits, e.g. Eye and skin colour (pigmented or non-pigmented), left-handed/right-handed, ability/inability to roll the tongue. Skin is a surface for some heat exchange and a barrier, but most large animals also need lungs or gills. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: If the environment does not change, then natural selection maintains populations or organisms so they do not change much over ____.
e: If the environment does not change, then natural selection maintains populations or organisms so they do not change much over time. The environment is everything around an organism, biotic and abiotic.

q: Natural selection will bring about a change to a species over time. Thus selection of adaptive variation is the mechanism by which ____ occurs.
e: Natural selection will bring about a change to a species over time. Thus selection of adaptive variation is the mechanism by which evolution occurs. A species is a group of organisms that can breed to produce fertile offspring.

q: Being adapted means being specialized to suit the environment in which organism ____.
e: Being adapted means being specialized to suit the environment in which organism lives. The environment is everything around an organism, biotic and abiotic.

q: Features which enable organisms to survive are called ____.
e: Features which enable organisms to survive are called adaptations. Adaptations are inherited traits that help survival in a given environment.

q: Adaptations can be classified as anatomical, physiological or ____.
e: Adaptations can be classified as anatomical, physiological or behavioural. Behavioural adaptations are things an animal does, such as seeking shade. Physiological adaptations are internal function changes, such as ADH control of water.

q: Anatomical adaptations are the structures of an organism that is modified to perform an adapted ____.
e: Anatomical adaptations are the structures of an organism that is modified to perform an adapted function. Function is what a structure does in the living body. Adaptations are inherited traits that help survival in a given environment.

q: Physiological adaptations are features of the processes inside an organism's body that increase its chance of survival or ____.
e: Physiological adaptations are features of the processes inside an organism's body that increase its chance of survival or reproduction. Physiological adaptations are internal function changes, such as ADH control of water. Adaptations are inherited traits that help survival in a given environment.

q: Behavioural adaptations are any actions by organisms which help them to survive or ____.
e: Behavioural adaptations are any actions by organisms which help them to survive or reproduce. Adaptations are inherited traits that help survival in a given environment. Behavioural adaptations are things an animal does, such as seeking shade.

q: Camels live and breed in desert, which is hottest, driest and most challenging ____.
e: Camels live and breed in desert, which is hottest, driest and most challenging environment. The environment is everything around an organism, biotic and abiotic.

q: Presence of closable nostrils and long eyelashes help keep out wind-blown ____.
e: Presence of closable nostrils and long eyelashes help keep out wind-blown sand. Sand is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Having large and flat feet with tough pads allows to spread out the weight of the camel as it walks over ____.
e: Having large and flat feet with tough pads allows to spread out the weight of the camel as it walks over sand. Sand is the biological term this statement needs.

q: The fatty tissue in the hump acts as food ____.
e: The fatty tissue in the hump acts as food store. Store is the biological term this statement needs.

q: As the fat is broken down to release energy during cellular respiration, water is produced as a ____.
e: As the fat is broken down to release energy during cellular respiration, water is produced as a by-product. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing. Viruses are not cellular.

q: The kidneys minimize the production of ____.
e: The kidneys minimize the production of urine. Urine is the waste fluid formed by nephrons. Kidneys excrete urea and regulate water and ions.

q: They sit down early in the morning before the ground warms up with their legs tucked underneath, so they can absorb a little heat from the ____.
e: They sit down early in the morning before the ground warms up with their legs tucked underneath, so they can absorb a little heat from the ground. An extra chromosome 21 produces Down's syndrome.

q: Groups of camels may lie down together, so that minimizing the amount of surface of each camel exposed to ____.
e: Groups of camels may lie down together, so that minimizing the amount of surface of each camel exposed to sun. An extra chromosome 21 produces Down's syndrome.

q: As they are browsers, they can eat a wide range of vegetation in desert, where carnivorous habit is ____.
e: As they are browsers, they can eat a wide range of vegetation in desert, where carnivorous habit is impossible. Impossible is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Natural selection is the process by which organisms that are well adapted to their environment have a greater chance to breed and pass on their alleles to the next ____.
e: Natural selection is the process by which organisms that are well adapted to their environment have a greater chance to breed and pass on their alleles to the next generation. The environment is everything around an organism, biotic and abiotic. Alleles are different versions of the same gene.

q: Forms that are not well adapted will not ____.
e: Forms that are not well adapted will not survive. Survive is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Beneficial mutations are the 'raw material' that are ultimately the source of new inherited ____.
e: Beneficial mutations are the 'raw material' that are ultimately the source of new inherited variation. Variation is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Artificial selection is the breeding of only those individuals with desired features as human choice, rather than environmental ____.
e: Artificial selection is the breeding of only those individuals with desired features as human choice, rather than environmental factors. Factors is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Artificial selection is also called ____.
e: Artificial selection is also called selective breeding. Selective breeding is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Farmers have bred crop plants of all kinds to obtain increased ____.
e: Farmers have bred crop plants of all kinds to obtain increased yield. Yield is the biological term this statement needs.

q: They selectively bred one species of wild brassica (Brassica oleracea) to give several strains, each with specific ____.
e: They selectively bred one species of wild brassica (Brassica oleracea) to give several strains, each with specific features. A species is a group of organisms that can breed to produce fertile offspring.

q: Modern selective breeding methods are cloning plants such as micropropagation and cloning animals by ____.
e: Modern selective breeding methods are cloning plants such as micropropagation and cloning animals by genetic modification. Modern biotechnology can move genes even between unrelated species.

q: Natural selection produces greater ____.
e: Natural selection produces greater biodiversity. Biodiversity is the variety of species, genes, and ecosystems.

q: Artificial selection produces varieties of organisms very different from native ____.
e: Artificial selection produces varieties of organisms very different from native generations. Generations is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Natural selection may lead to new ____.
e: Natural selection may lead to new species. A species is a group of organisms that can breed to produce fertile offspring.

q: Artificial selection does not result in new ____.
e: Artificial selection does not result in new species. A species is a group of organisms that can breed to produce fertile offspring.

q: In natural selection, outbreeding is common, leading to hybrid ____.
e: In natural selection, outbreeding is common, leading to hybrid vigour. Vigour is the biological term this statement needs.

q: In artificial selection, inbreeding is common, leading to loss of vigour in the ____.
e: In artificial selection, inbreeding is common, leading to loss of vigour in the offspring. Offspring is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Natural selection is a slow process, taking many ____.
e: Natural selection is a slow process, taking many years. Years is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Artificial selection is a relatively ____ process.
e: Artificial selection is a relatively fast process. Fast is the biological term this statement needs.

q: In natural selection, proportion of heterozygous individuals in the population remains ____.
e: In natural selection, proportion of heterozygous individuals in the population remains high. Heterozygous means the two alleles of a gene are different. A population is all the individuals of one species in an area.

q: In artificial selection, proportion of heterozygous individuals in the population is ____.
e: In artificial selection, proportion of heterozygous individuals in the population is reduced. Heterozygous means the two alleles of a gene are different. A population is all the individuals of one species in an area.

q: Nature refers to all of the genes and hereditary factors that influence physical characteristics of an ____.
e: Nature refers to all of the genes and hereditary factors that influence physical characteristics of an organism. Organism is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Nurture refers to all the environmental variables that impact on the ____.
e: Nurture refers to all the environmental variables that impact on the character. Character is the biological term this statement needs.

q: The basic characteristics of every individual are the result of the genes they have inherited from their ____.
e: The basic characteristics of every individual are the result of the genes they have inherited from their parents. Parents is the biological term this statement needs.

q: An apple tree seed will never grow into an oak ____.
e: An apple tree seed will never grow into an oak tree. Seed plants are gymnosperms and angiosperms.

q: Some differences between people are due entirely to the environment you live in. For example, you may have a scar as a result of an accident or an operation. Such variation is environmental, not ____.
e: Some differences between people are due entirely to the environment you live in. For example, you may have a scar as a result of an accident or an operation. Such variation is environmental, not genetic. The environment is everything around an organism, biotic and abiotic.

q: Genes play a major part in deciding how an organism will look but the conditions in which it develops are important ____.
e: Genes play a major part in deciding how an organism will look but the conditions in which it develops are important too. Too is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Features such as eye colour, nose shape, gender, and dimples are the results of genetic information inherited from ____.
e: Features such as eye colour, nose shape, gender, and dimples are the results of genetic information inherited from parents. Parents is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Genetically identical plants can be grown under different conditions of light or with different mineral ions. The resulting plants do not look identical. This shows their genetic potential have not been fully expressed, due to different ____ conditions.
e: Genetically identical plants can be grown under different conditions of light or with different mineral ions. The resulting plants do not look identical. This shows their genetic potential have not been fully expressed, due to different environmental conditions. Mitosis makes genetically identical body cells for growth and repair.
